## Executive Summary

## Problem

As of 2026, the International Seabed Authority (ISA) has **not finalized the mining code** governing commercial exploitation of polymetallic nodules in the Area—the seabed beyond national jurisdiction designated the "common heritage of humankind" under the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS, in force 16 November 1994) [8]. The draft Exploitation Regulations remain under active negotiation: the Council completed its second reading of the Revised Consolidated Text (Regulations 1–107) during the thirtieth session (March and July 2025), after which Decision ISBA/30/C/18 (18 July 2025) mandated a thematic approach and a Further Revised Consolidated Text for the thirty-first session [3]. Part II of that session (13–31 July 2026) continued deliberations amid intensifying controversy, with a growing coalition of ISA members and observers calling for a moratorium or precautionary pause until deep-sea ecosystem knowledge gaps are closed [8]. This regulatory vacuum sits at the intersection of two pressing imperatives: (i) protecting abyssal ecosystems from an activity never before conducted commercially, and (ii) securing critical mineral supply chains (cobalt, nickel, rare-earth elements) as a geopolitical hedge against concentrated Chinese processing dominance.
